ideas.hypothesis: Household survey respondents misreport their distance to schools, and the error is systematic: remote households understate distance. Self-reported distance therefore produces an attenuated (smaller) effect of school access on educational attainment than GPS-measured distance, so human capital stock estimates built from survey-based schooling models understate how much spatial access shapes the stock.

sources.role: method/mechanism: GPS in household surveys versus self-reported distance to roads, schools and services
method: estimating national human capital stock from household surveys (Dagum-Slottje)
measure: continuous sensor data on proximity and location as an objective record of behaviour
setting: demographic change that alters the age structure the stock is aggregated over
setting: ageing and socioeconomic change that alter spatial access to services

ideas.test: Use a household survey with both self-reported and GPS-derived distance to the nearest secondary school (for example an LSMS-type survey with geocoded households and schools). Measure the reporting error and how it correlates with remoteness. Estimate attainment regressions with each distance measure, instrumenting self-report with GPS, and recompute a Dagum-Slottje-style per-capita human capital value under each.
ideas.disconfirming: Self-reported and GPS distances give statistically indistinguishable attainment coefficients, or the reporting error is random noise that is unrelated to remoteness.

ideas.hypothesis: Higher-skilled workers search over thinner, more specialised labour markets and so commute over longer radii. Gravity or radiation mobility models with education-specific distance-decay parameters will therefore predict commuting flows out of sample more accurately than education-blind models, with the largest gains in cities where jobs are spatially mismatched with residents.

sources.role: setting/mechanism: spatial mismatch of employment opportunities in an urban labour market
method: mobility prediction models improved by assimilating auxiliary data
mechanism: returns to knowledge depend on interactive learning and environmental variables, not only individual schooling choice
mechanism: human capital quality determines regional economic activity and the ability to attract qualified personnel
setting: disaster-prone peripheral regions where mobility predictions are policy-relevant

ideas.test: Take census commuting origin-destination matrices broken down by educational attainment for one or two metro areas. Fit gravity and radiation models with pooled versus education-specific parameters on one census year, and compare prediction error (common part of commuters, RMSE) on held-out flows or the next census.
ideas.disconfirming: Education-specific parameters do not improve out-of-sample fit, or estimated commuting radii do not increase with education.

ideas.hypothesis: Capital account openness raises value-added growth in ICT-intensive industries more in countries with high human capital, because the two are complements. Capital flow management measures that restrict inflows therefore slow ICT-intensive industry growth mainly in high-human-capital economies.

sources.role: finding/method: human capital raises growth of ICT-intensive industries in open economies (industry-country panel)
setting: phased capital account opening and its risk management
mechanism: illicit capital flows as leakage that undermines formal capital flow management
measure: education and tertiary-industry indicators of human resource development

ideas.test: Industry-country panel (OECD STAN or UNIDO, 1990-2015) with ICT intensity by industry, Barro-Lee schooling, and a capital-control index (inflow restrictions). Estimate a Rajan-Zingales triple interaction: industry ICT intensity × country human capital × inflow controls, with country-year and industry-year fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: The triple interaction is zero or positive, meaning inflow controls do not hurt ICT-industry growth more in high-human-capital countries.

ideas.hypothesis: Human capital stock measures weighted by labour income (Mulligan and Sala-i-Martin style) build wage discrimination into the measured stock. Their divergence from schooling-based measures should therefore grow with the gender wage gap, and choosing between them changes growth-accounting conclusions about whose human capital counts.

sources.role: method: an income-share-weighted human capital stock based on educational attainment
method: an index system for measuring human capital's contribution to growth
mechanism: the ethics of allocation, where measurement choices decide whose needs are counted
finding: education level as a driver of ICT diffusion, an outcome to validate measures against
setting: Asian and Latin American growth comparisons where human capital measures matter

ideas.test: For a panel of 30-50 countries, compute both a schooling-years measure and an income-weighted measure of human capital stock. Regress the log ratio of the two on the gender wage gap (ILO or OECD data), then rerun a growth (or ICT-diffusion) regression with each measure and compare the coefficients.
ideas.disconfirming: The divergence between the measures is unrelated to the gender wage gap, and growth or ICT conclusions are identical under both measures.

ideas.hypothesis: Adolescents whose daily space-time prisms (the places they can reach within their time budgets) include physical activity facilities accumulate more health human capital, measured as cardiorespiratory fitness. Accessibility within these prisms predicts fitness better than straight-line distance from home.

sources.role: finding/measure: proximity to commercial activity facilities and fitness among adolescent girls
method: time geography and space-time constraints on activity participation
mechanism: urban form shapes walking and cycling activity patterns that affect health
mechanism: dynamic investment in human capital, here health as an investment good
setting: ICT-mediated services that relax space-time constraints

ideas.test: Recruit about 200 high-school students who wear GPS plus accelerometers for one week. Compute each student's space-time prism and the number of facilities reachable within it, plus straight-line home distance, and measure fitness with a shuttle-run test. Compare models predicting fitness from prism accessibility versus home distance, controlling for demographics.
ideas.disconfirming: Prism-based accessibility adds no explanatory power beyond home distance, or neither measure predicts fitness once vigorous activity is controlled.

ideas.hypothesis: Falling fertility raises the physical capital investment rate, through fewer dependents and more education per child, only where property rights are secure. In an augmented Solow panel, the interaction of fertility decline and property-rights protection on investment is positive and the main effect of fertility decline is small.

sources.role: method/mechanism: an augmented neoclassical (MRW) growth model in which property rights affect physical and human capital accumulation
mechanism: population ageing changes labour-force ratios and saving
setting: a declining birthrate in an ageing society
mechanism: majority-rule outcomes shift as the voter age distribution changes
mechanism: attitudes and behavioural theories that shape public investment planning

ideas.test: Country panel for 1970-2015 using five-year averages from the Penn World Table (investment share), World Bank total fertility rates, Barro-Lee schooling, and a property-rights index. Estimate system-GMM regressions of the investment rate on lagged fertility change, property rights, and their interaction.
ideas.disconfirming: Fertility decline raises investment equally regardless of property rights, or fertility decline does not raise investment at all.

ideas.hypothesis: In developing countries without capital flow management, surges in short-term capital inflows shift resources into non-tradables and real estate and lower the measured return to schooling and STEM enrollment, a human-capital Dutch disease. Countries with active inflow management measures show no such decline.

sources.role: mechanism: the IMF's shift toward accepting capital flow management for financial stability, viewed through Minsky-Kregel
mechanism: manpower (human) capital theory as central to development strategy in developing countries
mechanism: links between human capital, employment and income distribution
setting: capital account opening with risk early-warning and management frameworks

ideas.test: Panel of 30-40 emerging markets, 1995-2017, combining IMF-dated inflow-surge episodes, a capital-flow-management index, Mincerian returns to schooling from harmonised household surveys, and tertiary STEM enrollment shares. Run an event study of returns and enrollment around surges, split by whether capital flow management was in place.
ideas.disconfirming: Returns to schooling and STEM enrollment do not fall after surges, or they fall equally with and without capital flow management.

ideas.hypothesis: Post-disaster displacement predicted from mobility data, measured as the share of residents relocating outside the region, predicts larger subsequent remittance inflows. Through those remittances it also predicts faster rebuilding of housing and household physical capital, especially among financially excluded households that lack formal credit.

sources.role: method: deep learning prediction of emergency mobility from big heterogeneous data
finding: remittances rise after climatic and geological disasters (compensatory response)
mechanism/measure: financial exclusion and the link between remittances and livelihood assets, including physical capital
method: assimilating social media traces into mobility models
mechanism: congestion externalities that affect post-disaster recovery logistics

ideas.test: For two or three disasters with mobile-phone or social-media displacement estimates, link district-level predicted outflow shares to remittance receipts and housing reconstruction (from household panel surveys or permits) 6-24 months later. Interact with baseline bank-account ownership.
ideas.disconfirming: Predicted displacement does not predict remittances or rebuilding, or the link is no stronger for financially excluded households.

ideas.hypothesis: City districts where a larger share of clustered activity episodes take place at learning locations (universities, libraries, training centres), identified by spatio-temporal-semantic clustering of location data, show faster subsequent growth in tertiary-educated residents and in knowledge-intensive employment than formal enrollment statistics predict.

sources.role: method: three-step spatio-temporal-semantic clustering of human activity patterns
method: time geography as a framework for activity participation
measure: approaches to assessing regional structural change from capitalisation of intellectual potential
finding: intellectual capital as a determinant of labour productivity
mechanism: the rising role of the intellectual element in growth in the networked era

ideas.test: Cluster geotagged check-in or phone data for one large city in a base year to get each district's share of learning-related activity. Regress the 5-year change in districts' tertiary-attainment share and knowledge-intensive employment (census/business register) on that share, controlling for baseline enrollment and income.
ideas.disconfirming: The learning-activity share has no predictive power once baseline enrollment and income are controlled.

ideas.hypothesis: As a country's growth moves from physical capital accumulation toward human capital accumulation, its public research budgets shift from industrial and technology objectives toward health and education objectives. Countries that formally consult stakeholders when setting research priorities show this shift earlier and direct more funding toward the needs of disadvantaged groups.

sources.role: mechanism: the transition from physical to human capital accumulation as the engine of growth
mechanism/measure: equity and stakeholder engagement in research priority-setting
finding: factor accumulation with modest TFP growth, and trade in human capital during catch-up
setting: the shift from investment-based to innovation-based growth near the technology frontier
setting: technology-focused S&T priority-setting in emerging economies

ideas.test: OECD panel of government R&D budgets by socioeconomic objective (1990-2018), merged with growth-accounting shares of physical versus human capital contributions and a coded indicator of formal stakeholder engagement in national research priority-setting. Estimate a fixed-effects regression of the health/education budget share on the human capital share of growth and its interaction with engagement.
ideas.disconfirming: Budget composition is unrelated to the source of growth, or countries with stakeholder engagement show no earlier or larger shift.
